Connect Some is a free, open-source client for working with another machine from this phone. One app speaks three protocols: NVIDIA GameStream (NVStream, the protocol Moonlight implements), VNC (RFB) remote desktop, and ADB/scrcpy for Android devices. Whether the other end is a Windows PC, a Mac, a Linux box, a single-board computer or another phone, it is driven through the same gestures, the same keyboard, the same overlays and the same picture controls.

• VNC (RFB) connects to any standard VNC server. The authentication is chosen per server - automatic, none, VNC password, AnonTLS, VeNCrypt or Apple screen sharing - and an UltraVNC repeater can be put in front of it.
• GameStream (NVStream) is the Moonlight client, for a PC running Sunshine. Type in the PIN the host shows and the pairing is done; after that the desktop, or any single app on that PC, can be launched into the stream.
• ADB (scrcpy) mirrors and drives another Android device over wireless debugging or a USB-OTG cable. Nothing has to be installed on that device: a helper is copied to a temporary path and run from there, and it can be left running after you disconnect.
• All three share one set of gestures, keyboard, virtual keys, zoom rules, overlays and settings, instead of three apps with three different habits.
• Each saved server keeps its own picture and input settings, so a game stream and an office VNC session never have to agree on one compromise.
Finding a machine and reaching it

• A scan says which stage it is in - listening for announcements, walking the subnet, checking remote-desktop ports, looking up names, waiting for the late replies - and counts the machines it has found while it still runs.
• Announcements identify VNC, Apple screen sharing, Sunshine and LocalSend peers; a network that swallows multicast is covered by the manual subnet scan, and any machine can still be added by typing its address.
• A VPN that answers every probe is recognised: the scan then lists only the machines confirmed on the real local network, and explains why the list looks short.
• One machine answering on several ports of the same protocol is folded into a single card that names those ports.
• A card carries the name, the address, the model, and the MAC address the scan learned; it can be copied, saved, or saved with the Wake-on-LAN fields already filled in.
• Wake-on-LAN has its own button on every card. The MAC address can be looked up by the app, and the broadcast address can be derived from the target IPv4 address.
• Search matches only the fields you switch on: name, address, protocol, port, MAC, broadcast address and port, username.
• A saved server can demand the device credential before it connects, reconnect on its own after a dropped link, be merged with the duplicates a scan produced, and be opened from a home-screen shortcut.
• A vnc://, moonlight:// or android:// link may arrive from a browser or a QR code, but only after a dialog has shown where it points - a stray link should not open a remote session by itself.
• A server whose certificate is new or has changed is put in front of you instead of being accepted or refused in silence.

• Resolution, frame rate and bitrate are set per server for GameStream and ADB. RFB instead has a quality step from 0 to 9 and a switch that insists on raw, uncompressed updates, because the protocol itself has no bitrate and no frame rate to expose.
• Per server you can also let the remote desktop resize itself to the stream, connect as soon as an app starts, delay a mouse-button release, and pick the orientation and the gesture style.
• Zoom has a lower and an upper limit, an optional default for each screen orientation, a lock, a reset, and one button that saves the current zoom as the default. The area behind the picture takes any color you choose.
• Three view modes: normal, input disabled, and picture only with every input ignored - the last one for watching a machine without touching it.
• Picture-in-picture keeps the stream going in a corner while you use other apps.
• Remote audio plays on this phone and can be muted here without affecting the other machine; the VNC bell can be turned into a short beep on this phone.
• A switchable overlay reports frame rate and latency for as long as the session lasts.
• Decoding can pause while the app is in the background to save battery, and on GameStream and ADB the frames can go straight to the display surface instead of making the round trip through the GL renderer, which saves a few milliseconds.

• Two gesture models, chosen app-wide or per server: touchscreen, where a touch acts where it lands, and touchpad, where the finger drives a pointer. One-, two- and three-finger taps, double tap, long press, a swipe in each of those, double-tap-and-swipe and long-press-and-swipe can each be bound to an action of their own - the four kinds of click, a press, moving the pointer, panning the local frame, scrolling or dragging the remote content, a back press, opening the keyboard.
• A real mouse can be passed through to the server untouched, or captured so that its relative motion moves the remote pointer while the local cursor hides. The mouse back button can be remapped, and the swipe sensitivity says how far one swipe drags the pointer.
• The local pointer marker draws an arrow or a dot, at any size and in any color, exactly where your finger lands - so a session driven by touch is not a guess.
• The virtual-key row can sit at the top or at the bottom, be one to three rows deep, and be filled key by key from a picker laid out like a real keyboard: modifiers, navigation, punctuation, letters, numbers, function keys, numpad, media keys, and the actions that end the session or open the menu. It can also appear whenever the phone keyboard opens.
• A full QWERTY keyboard covers the picture for typing with touch alone, with adjustable size and transparency, a position lock, and a handle that lets it be pushed partly off screen while staying reachable.
• Key mappings bend a phone keyboard towards a desktop: right Alt to Super, the language-switch key to Super, Back to Escape.
• Text can be sent while it is typed or once the word is confirmed - the difference between an editor that keeps up and a field that swallows half of a composition.
• The clipboard is shared in both directions, with a strict Latin-1 mode that reads the classic VNC field exactly as the protocol defines it, and with a size limit you can raise for ADB, whose 5000-byte packet drops a longer copy without a word.

• An assist ball hovers over the stream at any size, color and transparency, and opens the toolbar or the keyboard when tapped.
• A drawer slides in from an edge, and the width of the band that catches that swipe is yours to set, so it opens when you mean it and not by accident. Which buttons it carries, and in what order, is edited by dragging; every panel inside it can be restored to its defaults on its own.
• The mini window floats the stream above any other app: drag it, resize it from the two dots on its bottom bar or from either bottom corner, collapse it against the edge, rotate the remote screen, reach the phone keys and the power menu, or blank the remote display and leave the sound running.
• Every button of the mini window is assignable - three slots on the top bar and a double tap on the bottom - and the Back / Home / Recents row is switched per protocol, because only a device driven over ADB can receive those keys.
• Opening a mini window starts a fresh stream, so it is another way of looking at the machine rather than a way of keeping a session alive. Its first size follows the phone itself instead of the picture, so a stream that had no side bars in full screen has none inside the card either.
• Messages that pop up inside the stream have an adjustable transparency and go away at the first touch, so they cannot sit on a button you want.

• Files, or a message typed on the spot, go to any nearby device that speaks the LocalSend protocol, so the other end can be a computer, another phone or a tablet running any LocalSend app.
• Switching it on also makes this phone discoverable and willing to accept. An offer coming in is asked about before anything is written away, and the message says which folder a received file landed in.
• Picked files wait in a queue, because the machine they belong to is often not switched on yet. Tapping a device sends the queue to it, and the same batch can go on to the next device afterwards.
• Devices can be pinned as favorites, renamed, put in order by dragging, and used even while discovery has not confirmed them; one that never announces itself can be added by IP address.
• A batch can be handed out as a download link instead, which any device on the same network opens in a browser. Live links stay listed rather than vanishing with the dialog that made them, and each can be copied, shared, given another file, stripped of one, or revoked.
• That link is served by this phone on the local network. It is not a link for the internet, and it is refused when there is no Wi-Fi or hotspot address to serve it from.
• The search for peers says how far it has got, as a percentage with a done/total count, and can be stopped halfway.

• Export and import write one file that you keep, and every part of it is a switch of its own: servers, settings, LocalSend favorites, the addresses and MAC addresses a scan learned, known SSH hosts and trusted certificates, passwords and keys, and the GameStream pairing certificate.\n• Backup protection can require the device credential for anything that holds secrets - including for throwing that switch itself, so a reset cannot quietly turn into a way around it. Restoring every setting leaves the saved servers alone and leaves that switch alone.\n• Log capture can be off, kept for this launch, or kept across launches; the log can be read, exported or cleared. Two debugging screens record every touch event and every key translation, so an input problem can be pinned to this app or to the other machine with the log in hand.

• The theme follows the system or is forced light or dark, and the interface color is picked on a color wheel or typed as a code; both variants are derived from that one color.
• The language of the app is chosen inside it, independently of the system language, and applies immediately. Besides English there are 22 translations, and a sentence one of them has not covered falls back to English instead of showing nothing.
• The badge on a card names the protocol behind it, and those three names can be replaced by a preset or by a word of your own.
• Saved servers can be listed in name order instead of the order in which they were added.

• SSH tunneling is not implemented. An entry that asks to be reached through a tunnel is refused rather than connected without one, because that would put the password on an unencrypted link; the editor says so and switches the entry back to a direct connection.
• VNC quality is the 0 to 9 scale, since the protocol has no bitrate and no frame rate to expose, and direct-scan rendering does nothing on VNC.
• The ADB protocol has no key release: every key arrives as a short press, so a held key, auto-repeat and a chord of modifiers are out of reach. A character with no key code is written to the other device clipboard instead.
• One device serves one ADB client at a time, so a computer running adb or scrcpy against the same phone takes the connection away from this app.
• The windows that float above other apps - the mini window, the LocalSend floating window, the assist ball - need the draw-over-other-apps permission, which Android only lets you grant by hand on a system screen.
• VNC and the ADB wireless pairing live in optional native components. A build made without one says so on the screen where it would have been used instead of failing quietly, and the cable keeps working.
• GameStream needs a host that still speaks it, which in practice means a computer running Sunshine, since NVIDIA ended GameStream support on newer hardware.
• This app runs on Android 8.0 and newer.

• Connect Some merges several existing open-source projects instead of writing any of the protocols again: AVNC by Gaurav Ujjwal supplies the VNC (RFB) client, the server-profile model and most of the settings screens; Moonlight by the moonlight-stream team supplies the GameStream client, its decoder path and its controller model; Easycontrol_For_Car by Eiyooooo supplies the ADB transport and the helper it runs on the other device; and Ning by csicar and Duorem supply parts of the scan - active mDNS probing, the MAC-vendor table and the NetBIOS lookup.\n• Written for this app on top of them: LocalSend with its favorites and its download links, the mini window in the style of Mi-Freeform\'s freeform windows, the assist ball and the drawer, the rest of the network scan, the pointer marker and the server behind the links.\n• Like the projects it is built from, it is released under the GNU General Public License, version 3 or later. The libraries it stands on - LibVNCClient, moonlight-common-c with its enet, libjpeg-turbo, jMDNS, Bouncy Castle, libadb-android, OkHttp, jcodec, AndroidX, Material and Room - carry notices of their own, collected in docs/ThirdPartyLicenses.md of the source.

ADB only: the controlled device and this app each cap one clipboard packet at 5000 bytes, which quietly drops a longer copy. Set your own cap instead - it is sent to the device, so both directions keep working.
1 to 65535 bytes. A value outside that range is moved back inside. Text is counted in UTF-8 bytes, so one Chinese character costs three.

Ctrl, Alt, Shift and Super stay pressed after a single tap until you tap them again. A key typed after them fires once and leaves the modifier held.

Marks the coordinate this app sends to the computer, with the tip or the center of the mark exactly on it. Over VNC the server confirms where its pointer really is; over GameStream nothing comes back, so the mark shows the position a touch was mapped to. When the desktop is a different size than the stream - bands added by the host, for instance - a fixed residual offset stays possible, and the dot shape or the size slider is the way around it.
The arrow as a percentage of its default size.
